summary: Beer & Bread is a compact two-player card game where you alternate managing a beer village and a bread village across a series of years, drafting and playing multi-use cards to build production while denying your neighbor the same resources. It plays fast but rewards careful sequencing, since a single card can serve as a resource, a building, or a scoring asset depending on how it's used.
praised: Clever multi-use card design that rewards efficient sequencing
Fast, tight two-player experience with real head-to-head tension
Good production and component quality for a small-box game
criticised: Can feel dry or overly mechanical given the farming theme
Some randomness in card draws affects available options
Limited long-term variety once the system is learned

interaction.detail: The two villages draw from and compete over shared fields and resource availability, so choices about what to take or build affect what remains for the other player. Each player still develops their own private tableau of buildings and production, but scoring categories are compared directly against each other at game end.

scoring.why: Final scoring cross-compares each player's beer total against the opponent's bread total (and vice versa), so being strong where your rival is weak is what swings the result.
scoring.how_you_win: Harvest and process resources into beer and bread across six alternating years, then at game end your beer is scored against your opponent's bread and your bread against their beer; whoever comes out ahead in that cross-comparison wins.
